hair: black, thick and straight, worn in a long braid down her spine or loose past her shoulders; she winds it up when concentrating
complexion: warm golden-bronze undertone, a faint scar along her left collarbone from a childhood fall on ice
face: a wide, open face with high cheekbones and a broad mouth—the kind of face that broadcasts feeling before thought catches up, dark eyes that go soft when she's uncertain and flash when she's angry
signature_feature: her hands—long-fingered, deft, with a tremor of life in them; the LI notices how they move when she talks, how they shake when she's afraid, how steady they become when she's making something
second_celebrated_feature: the small hollow at the base of her throat, visible when her neck is exposed; the LI finds himself watching it rise and fall when she breathes, when she's nervous, when she's trying not to cry
signature_habits: she braids her hair when anxious—methodical, repetitive, grounding
she speaks to herself in Inuktitut when concentrating on detail work, half-aware she's doing it
she eats seal oil on her bread without thinking, the taste a wordless anchor to her grandmother's kitchen
she touches the scar on her collarbone when lying or hearing a lie—a tell she doesn't know she has
she goes very still before asking for something she needs, holding her breath like she's bracing for no
occupation: textile artist and small-studio owner in the city; she designs and hand-dyes traditional-inspired fabrics and sells them to high-end boutiques; her studio is her sanctuary and her livelihood

current_crisis.event: her studio's landlord—a property developer with billionaire backing—has given her 60 days to vacate; the building is being demolished for luxury condos; she has no savings buffer, no backup location, and the LI is somehow entangled in the developer's world
current_crisis.hottest_emotion: panic masked as numbness; a creeping sense of erasure
current_crisis.immediate_want: to find a new space she can afford and save her work before the deadline; to NOT have to ask for help

wound.core: she believes that needing someone is the same as being disposable—that the moment she admits dependence, she becomes a burden and will be left
wound.surfacing_hint: when afraid or cornered, she becomes hyperindependent and refuses help even when drowning; she'll sabotage a relationship rather than risk being abandoned first; she flinches when someone notices her struggling
